title: A plasma delay curve gives no clear prediction gain for middle components in 97 selected CHIME events
abstract: We test a residual cold-plasma delay relation in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, release 20251231. First and last components set each curve; 147 middle components in 97 events test its predictions. With equal source weights, mean absolute error is 26.94 MHz for the plasma curve and 25.60 MHz for a straight frequency trend. The difference is +1.34 MHz, with a nominal 95 percent source resample interval from -0.31 to +2.95 MHz. A joint quality control retains 51 events and no clear plasma gain. The median difference between model predictions is 2.43 MHz. Conditional simulations test independent middle noise with exact endpoints. Missing peak errors, joint fit covariance, beam response, and component selection prevent a physical rejection or confirmation. We add a prediction comparison to prior campaign plasma tests. No new source or planet is found. The package contains original code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes, and retrieval steps. External catalog rows and record tables remain outside the baseline publication. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-3b69916f3d20; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Middle component prediction errors and source resample intervals. Positive differences favor the straight frequency trend. Intervals exclude measurement and model errors.
Conditional simulations compare the sign of mean error under independent middle frequency noise. Endpoints and times are exact. These fractions are not detection power at a fixed false-positive rate.
